TF mechanobiological regulation pathway

TF mechanobiological regulation pathway. (a) Mechanical cues within the tumor microenvironment, including ECM stiffening, interstitial flow, and compression, activate mechanoreceptors such as integrins and PIEZO1 channels [36, 37]. Notably, the engagement of tissue factor (TF) with factor VIIa (FVIIa) facilitates the formation of a high-affinity complex that associates with activated integrins, anchoring the procoagulant machinery at the membrane and priming cells for thrombotic signaling [38]. (b) Mechanotransduction activates multiple intracellular cascades. Integrin-FAK-SRC signaling initiates Hippo-independent YAP/TAZ nuclear translocation, while FAK also stimulates PI3K/AKT/mTOR and MAPK/ERK pathways [39–45]. Concurrently, PIEZO1-mediated Ca²⁺ influx activates PKC and calcineurin, promoting NFAT dephosphorylation and nuclear translocation [46, 47]. Together, these pathways converge on the TF promoter, amplifying its transcription. (c) Newly synthesized TF is transported from the Golgi through vesicular trafficking pathways to the plasma membrane. A subset of TF is packaged into EVs, while others are inserted into the membrane surface for coagulation engagement [35, 38, 48]. (d) TF is surface-presented in an encrypted (non-coagulant) state. Mechanical and biochemical cues induce the exposure of phosphatidylserine (PS) and disruption of sphingomyelin, decrypting TF and enabling complex formation with FVIIa and FXa, thereby initiating extrinsic coagulation [49, 50].
